text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Moslem-Croat Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic says polling stations which were opened in the federation for presidential election in neighbouring Croatia were illegal.

- Voting for the Croatian president on Bosnian territory will have a negative effect on a meeting between Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and Moslem chairman of collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, scheduled for June 23 in Croatia, commentary says.

- Federation Transport Minister Rasim Gacanovic proposes construction of highways and other public works projects to address unemployment problem. There are some 700,000 unemployed in the Moslem-Croat federation and the situation in the country's Serb republic is even worse, he says.

- Because partners in the Moslem-Croat federation could not agree on forming new municipalities, some 67,000 voters will not be able to cast their ballots in local elections, says Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.

- Bosnian Serbs prevent 216 Moslem families from returning to their homes in two suburbs in Doboj. A Nordic-Polish patrol from the NATO-led peace force was stoned by an angry Serb crowd, NATO officer says. -- Sarajevo Newsroom 387 71 663 864
